one_liner: Write and run a complete, resumable single-GPU pretraining loop with real throughput monitoring.

key_terms.definition: Achieved FLOPs/s divided by the accelerator's peak FLOPs/s; the metric that measures true compute efficiency, unlike misleading GPU-Util percentages.
Summing gradients over several micro-batches before one optimizer step, so the effective batch size (micro-batch × seq_len × accum steps) exceeds what fits in memory at once.
Training with bfloat16's 8-bit exponent (fp32's dynamic range, fewer mantissa bits) inside a torch.autocast region, avoiding fp16's overflow risk and need for loss scaling.
Approximation that one forward-plus-backward training pass costs about 6 FLOPs per parameter per token, used to convert measured tokens/sec into achieved FLOPs/s for MFU.
Memory-saving technique that discards intermediate activations during the forward pass and recomputes them during backward, trading ~30% more compute for a large reduction in activation memory.
Rescaling the gradient vector across all parameters jointly (not per-tensor) so its L2 norm does not exceed a threshold, catching model-wide gradient explosions before the optimizer step.
Saving model weights, optimizer state, step counter, data-loader cursor, and RNG states atomically so a training run can be exactly resumed after an interruption.
A PaLM-style auxiliary penalty on the squared log-sum-exp of the logits, added to cross-entropy loss to stabilize training by discouraging unbounded logit growth.
A learning-rate schedule with a short linear warmup, a long constant plateau, and a short final decay phase, used here to set the per-step learning rate during training.
A single dataclass fixing every run-mechanics number (batch sizes, optimizer hyperparameters, logging/checkpoint cadence) for a pretraining run, itself checkpointed to prevent config drift on resume.

A multi-GPU scale-out technique that replicates the model on every GPU, runs independent micro-batches, and all-reduces gradients before each optimizer step, reducing wall-clock but not total compute.
A multi-GPU technique that shards parameters, gradients, and optimizer state across GPUs (à la ZeRO) instead of replicating them, trading communication for reduced per-GPU memory footprint.

prerequisites: the optimizer and WSD learning-rate schedule (Muon+AdamW)
